## Bet 6 — Camera cutout without a green screen, and camera layouts

Prefix CO. Phases CO0, CO1, CO2a, CO2b, CO3…CO10; CO2a and CO2b share CO2's decision block
(CJ-7). Phase COn owns decisions CO-n0…CO-n9 (CO0 owns CO-1…CO-9). Spikes CO-S1…CO-S4. Manual
checks JOB-60…JOB-65 (numbers provisional; the integrator renumbers). Format bumps are written
"format N (provisional)": RC_FORMAT_VERSION is 37 at `d0661e5d` (`core/src/format.rs:18`), and each
bump is renumbered when its phase lands (CJ-6). Handoff directories are
`~/.claude/litecode/framejob/cj-co0`, `cj-co1`, `cj-co2a`, `cj-co2b`, `cj-co3` … `cj-co10`.

### Goal

A creator who records themselves gets four things on the camera clip that today need a green
screen or another app.

- **Remove Background.** One checkbox on a camera clip cuts the person out of their room. The
  segmentation runs on the Mac through Apple's Vision framework, on the road map's analysis lane,
  and is cached in the package. The edge can be shrunk, grown and softened. The drop shadow
  follows the person's outline. The camera keeps everything else Frame Job gives a clip: grading,
  LUTs, Camera Log, HDR, actions.
- **Text Behind Subject.** A title sits between the person and their background: the person's
  head passes in front of the words. It works over the camera's own room and over a screen
  recording behind a cut-out camera.
- **Camera layouts.** Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸ and a Layout section switch the camera at the
  playhead, with an eased move, between a corner picture (square, rounded or a circle), side by
  side, stacked for a vertical canvas, camera full and screen only. Each switch is an ordinary
  action on the camera clip and the screen clip, which the creator can drag, retime or delete on
  the action lane. The recorder offers the same layout at record time, and can land the camera
  with its background removed.
- **Hide the camera while silent.** The camera fades out while the microphone is silent and back
  in before speech resumes, read from the speech spans Frame Job already detects on the Mac.

Every control has an MCP mirror, so "put me in a circle bottom-left from 1:20, and hide me while I
type" is a sentence an agent can carry out in the calls a person's clicks make.

### Owner's answers applied

The owner's answers of 2026-11-01, as the orchestrator reads them for this bet. Each is a default
the owner can change.

- **"Add all: 1-6."** Bet 6 is in, as phases CO0…CO10 of road map "creator-jobs", in lane B after
  CU's phases (cj.md "Lane plan").
- **"Remove all explicit non-goals."** CJ-1 lifts spec §1's "ML or heavy pixel work outside the
  compositor's one pass". This bet uses the lift: Vision analysis on the analysis lane, and a
  mask sampled in the layer pass. Shipping or downloading a matting model is allowed by CJ-1 and
  is not built here; it becomes a filed candidate only if the owner's verdict on Vision's edges
  (JOB-60) is "not good enough". One licence fact bounds that candidate: Frame Job is
  Apache-2.0 (`LICENSE`), so code or weights under GPL-3.0 (Robust Video Matting's release) or
  AGPL (Concat's) cannot ship in it. That is a fact about licences, not a scope rule. Optical
  flow and stabilisation are allowed by CJ-1; nothing here needs them.
- **"The recorder can ask for input monitoring."** Not used by this bet. The recorder's camera
  rows gain a Layout pop-up and a checkbox (CO8), and neither needs a new grant.
- **The key rule (CJ-3).** Nothing in this bet needs a language model or a cloud model. Person
  segmentation is Vision on the Mac, which CJ-3 lists with Sound Analysis, Speech and Silero VAD
  as not "significant AI": it needs no key and is never disabled for want of one. Hide while
  silent reads Silero VAD's spans (`media.speech`, spec §11 AU-110). No control in this bet is
  greyed for a missing key, and no tool of this bet is in `ModelKeys.keyed`.
- **"Cutting one real video per lead segment … alongside the first bet."** The trial is CJ-5's: T1
  from S-TH1 and T2 from S-ST1, its verdict recorded under CJ-5. This bet records its own person
  checks, JOB-60…JOB-64, against S-TH1 and S-ST1, with each verdict written into CO's phase
  record the way grading recorded GR-9.

### How it fits the tree

Facts read at `d0661e5d`. Line counts are `wc -l`.

**Nothing exists yet.** No Vision import is in `app/Sources`. `cutout` appears nowhere in
`core/src` or `app/Sources`. Issue #124 (Effects E9, iceboxed) holds the earlier design and the
proposed decision D5, which was never entered in §11. Its spike is
`tools/proof/effects_spike/vision_{common,stills,job}.swift` and `vision_fixtures.sh`, with the
measurements in `archive/effects-survey.md` §5b and `designs/adr/effects-survey.md:264–285,
326–334`:

- `VNGeneratePersonSegmentationRequest` is synchronous through `VNImageRequestHandler` and needs no
  grant. Masks are always 4:3 whatever the input: fast 256×192, balanced 512×384, accurate
  2016×1512, stretched over the frame in normalised coordinates, y down.
- Warm medians at 1080p: fast 6.6 ms, balanced 28.3 ms, accurate 65.1 ms. E9 chose `.balanced` at
  10 masks per second of source, which runs 4.2–5.5× realtime; accurate runs 1.6–1.7×.
- One device is byte-identical across runs and processes; GPU and ANE differ by up to 25 levels.
  `.fast` is stateful; balanced and accurate are not.
- Person coverage on UI, text and cards is 0.00 %. Foreground instance masks flip up to 57 % of
  pixels on a slow push-in, so they are for stills only.
- Not measured: real camera footage, hair, motion blur, the first-ever Neural Engine compile.
- The issue's `texture(2)` is stale. Its own last comment says the cutout takes `texture(4)`.

**Availability.** `VNGeneratePersonSegmentationRequest` (macOS 12), `VNGeneratePersonInstanceMaskRequest`
and `VNGenerateForegroundInstanceMaskRequest` (macOS 14) and `VNRequest.setComputeDevice(_:for:)`
(macOS 14) all exist on the minimum, macOS 26 (spec §11 W-8). The newer Swift `Vision` request
structs are `async`-only and are not used, because `async` is confined to `MediaImporter.swift` and
`SpeechEngine.swift` (W-8). The `VN*` classes are what the spike ran.

**The analysis lane is CJ2a's.** CJ-20…CJ-27 (cj.md) give the road map one lane (`AnalysisLane`,
width 1 unless CJ-S3 earns 2, `.utility`), one store (`cache/analysis/<kind>/<media id>.json` plus
payload files, runs over source spans in media source ticks, an `AnalysisStamp` with no path, the
OS build and the compute device, written only through `CacheLedger.publish`), one frame reader
(display orientation; the thumbnails' converted path for converting media), one tool
(`get_media_analysis`), canned markers for proofs (`-RCDevAnalysisCanned YES`) and one Analyzing
sheet (CJ2b). CJ-20 already names CO's masks as "a render drawn from [analysis] … substituted by
Swift, as a reversed file is". CJ-8 (c) puts every analysis kind under `cache/analysis/<kind>/`.
This bet's masks are such a kind. Where a mask needs something the shared design does not give,
this section amends the CJ entry in writing (CO-4, CO-6, CO-7, CO-9).

**The compositor has one free texture slot reserved for this bet.** The layer fragment function
binds `texture(0)` source, `texture(1)` matte coverage, `texture(2)` look lattice, `texture(3)`
curves strip (`app/Resources/Shaders/Compositor.metal:1902–1906`, 2811 lines). CJ-8 (b) reserves
`texture(4)` for CO's layer mask. Coverage is multiplied at step 7b (corner radius) and 7c
(matte), `Compositor.metal:1771–1795`. `LayerUniforms` is 132 floats, 528 bytes, 33 × 16
(`Compositor.metal:381`; `LayerUniforms.swift:245–250`); a new field adds a group of four, and
CJ-8 (b) appends groups in landing order. The shadow's silhouette pass binds the same slots
(`Compositor+Shadow.swift:221–230`), which is why a matte's cut already shapes a shadow (MT-3).
Every video source decodes to `64RGBAHalf` (`Compositor.swift:147`). In a `ConvertingCompositor`
a source frame "arrives native and labelled, and step 0 converts it"
(`Compositor.swift:150–152`; `Compositor+Input.swift:19`, `:190–191`), per layer. The layer stage
samples a source at `orientedUV(uv, …)` (`Compositor.metal:406`, used at `:805`): `uv` is in
display space and `orientedUV` maps it to the coded texture.

**A layer's picture is a composition track.** The recipe's media and still source is `{kind:
"track", track_id}` (`core/src/recipe.rs:464–479`, 547 lines); an image takes another arm
(`:480–`). The track is chosen by `Assignment.video_of`, keyed by instance path
(`core/src/evaluate.rs:433–490`, 559 lines). The recipe publishes no source time.
`recipe_layer.rs` (158) is the one writer of a layer's twenty-six keys (`recipe_layer.rs:14`). The
plan warns past eight concurrent video tracks and never refuses (`core/src/plan.rs:19`, 294).
`CompositionBuilder.fill` (`CompositionBuilder.swift:285–330`, 546 lines) inserts one source range
per segment and scales it, behind a cursor.

**A reversed clip reads another file, chosen beside the plan.** `CompositionBuilder.build` reads
`ReverseSource.shared.resolution(for:)` (`CompositionBuilder.swift:120`), and `fill` substitutes
the reversed file per CLIP, with the segment's source range measured in the reversed stream
(`:291–303`). A clip with no file yet gets empty time and draws the slate. The core keeps no
mirror (spec §11 D4-6); `ReverseMirror.swift` is the app's one spelling of it.
`ReverseResolution` (`ReverseCache.swift`, 365) carries the ramp, isolation and voice render
folders, so the export's capture and pin carry them with no change of their own; `voiced` is
computed from `cache`.

**Offline renders have one shape.** `RampAudioRenders.swift` (281) is a process-wide serial queue
with owners that want files, renames into place inside `CacheLedger.publish`, and a `settled`
closure that posts `.reversedMediaDidChange` so the frozen editor rebuilds. The document's wants
are `ensureRampAudio()` (`ProjectDocument+RampAudio.swift:40`, 84 lines), which
`ProjectDocument.swift` (1336, over the cap) already calls after an open (`:456`), a reverse
landing (`:974`) and every edit (`:1273`). The export waits in `Exporter.withRampAudio`
(`Exporter+RampAudio.swift:23`, 141 lines) and releases its wants in `releaseRecipeKey`
(`Exporter.swift:447–455`; the file is 598). `Exporter.renderFrame` (`Exporter.swift:525`) does
not wait; its callers are `render_frame`, Save Frame (`EditorViewController+SaveFrame.swift:201`,
399 lines), the eyedropper (`EditorViewController+Eyedropper.swift:228`) and the look gallery
(`LookGallery.swift:193`). `BackgroundRender.swift` (116) knows every transport and whether one
plays.

**Mattes already cut one layer by another layer's picture.** `recipe_matte.rs` (219) emits each
layer's `matte: {into, cut}` and the frame's `mattes` groups; `Compositor+Matte.swift` (316) and
`MattePlan.swift` (73) draw each group into a pooled destination-sized target and resolve each cut
set into one `r8Unorm` coverage at `texture(1)` (spec §11 MT-3, MT-6, MT-9). A matte group today
comes only from a matte TRACK (MT-1).

**Placement and actions.** (★) in `core/src/edit_zoom.rs` (467) is the one placement rule, solved
there for a region; `add_zoom_action` composes `add_action` + `set_action_end` into one step.
`edit_fit.rs` (61) holds `fit_scale`, a rescue that never scales up and honours
`canvas.fit_new_clips` (`edit_fit.rs:19`), and `fill_scale`. Actions on one clip may not overlap
(spec §5.4). Numbers, crops and corner radius interpolate; strings and booleans switch at the end.
**Actions carry no tag**: `Action {id, start, duration, curve, end}` (`core/src/model.rs:440`).
The only zoom test is `ActionBands.isZoom` (`app/Sources/ActionBands.swift:37–43`): an end whose
`video` keys are exactly `scale`, `x` and `y`. CU-5 recognises zooms by content and CU7 adds the
core's twin (cu.md). A nest clip folds only x, y, scale, rotation, opacity and its crop as a
clipping rect; its corner radius and every per-pixel key reach no layer
(`core/src/nest.rs:382–394`, 470).

**The recorder's camera corner is Swift arithmetic.** `RecordingLanding+Camera.swift:35–66` (255)
computes CAM-10 (3)'s box (a quarter of the canvas wide, a third tall, inset 5 %) and writes one
`set_video {x, y, scale}` on the camera, nothing on the screen. The camera lands on a new front
track named "Camera" (`:34`). The screen lands on the container's EXISTING front track when it
fits (`RecordingLanding.swift:252–268`), so later clips on that track are clips the person placed
before recording. The recorder panel has eleven `FrameJobRecording…` keys, persisted in
`RecorderPanelController+Rows.swift` (395 of 400) from `:271`, among them
`FrameJobRecordingCameraBeside` (CAM-11). The dev tool `land_recording` lands fixture files
through either door (AU-69).

**Speech spans live on the media.** `media.speech` (format 29, AU-110) is written by
`set_media_speech` from the Silero VAD cache (`DuckSpeech.swift`, 153); `speech_in_clip`
(`core/src/audio_duck_speech.rs:31`, 193) maps them into a clip's own time through reversal,
speed and ramps. The `set_audio` tool prepends `DuckSpeech.ops` when a patch sets `duck.mode`
to `speech` (`AgentServer+Properties.swift:59–80`). The timeline's duck line is the frozen
`TimelineView.swift`'s one stored property `duckCurves` (`:35`), set at
`EditorViewController+Timeline.swift:75` and drawn from `TimelineClipDrawing.swift:129`. sw.md's
SW-42 adds `media.audio_speech` per stream.

**Files at or over the cap that this bet touches or avoids**, with the toll each pays (the
"Tolls" table under CO0 says which phase pays):

- `app/Sources/ProjectSnapshot.swift` 1454: CU0's toll 6 moves `VideoProps` out whole to
  `VideoProps.swift`; CO's fields land there.
- `core/src/edit_action.rs` 595: the end-patch door (`prune_removed` … `key_off`, `:104–291`; the
  `not_a_target` refusals `:181–186`) out to `edit_action_end.rs` (cj.md: "VR or CO, whichever
  first"; vr.md says VR takes nothing from it).
- `core/src/actions.rs` 587: the named seam `color_json`, `wheels_json`, `video_json` →
  `actions_json.rs` (cj.md: CO), only if a phase's wiring would pass ~590.
- `core/src/recipe.rs` 547: CJ0 T3 moves the content hash to `recipe_hash.rs`.
- `core/src/evaluate.rs` 559: the proposed `Segment` cut → `plan_segment.rs` (cj.md: SW), paid by
  CO2a only if `mask_of` would take the file past ~590 and SW has not paid it.
- `core/src/props_check.rs` 550: avoided; CO's checks live in `cutout_check.rs`, one call line
  per phase.
- `core/src/format_history.rs` 371 of 400: four CO bumps add paragraphs; the bump that would pass
  400 pays cj.md's proposed cut (versions 2–24 → `format_history_early.rs`), unless another lane
  has.
- `app/Sources/AgentCatalog+Properties.swift` 410: `videoPatchDescription` (`:160`) grows in
  CO2a, CO5, CO9 and CO10; the video patch's clauses (`:23–191`) move out first.
- `app/Sources/Exporter.swift` 598: the export's mask wait goes inside `withRampAudio`; the
  frame's wait and report go in `// MARK: - Offline single frame` (`:478–598`) after it moves to
  `Exporter+Frame.swift` (cj.md: CO); `releaseRecipeKey` takes one line.
- `app/Sources/EditorViewController+SaveFrame.swift` 399 of 400: its `// MARK: - The save panel's
  options` (`:277–399`) moves out before Save Frame reports a pending cutout.
- `app/Sources/ProjectDocument.swift` 1336: avoided; the mask wants are called from inside
  `ensureRampAudio()`.
- `app/Sources/VideoPane.swift` 871: avoided; every new section is a new file registered in
  `ClipPane.makeSections()` (`ClipPane.swift:192–205`, 266).
- `app/Sources/RecorderPanelController+Rows.swift` 395: CU0's toll 3 moves the persisted choice
  out to `RecorderPanelController+Choices.swift`; CO8's rows come after it.
- `app/Sources/FrameRecipe.swift` 417: CU0's toll 5 moves the matte types out; `RecipeLayer.cutout`
  comes after it.
- `app/Sources/CompositionBuilder.swift` 546: CJ0 T6 moves the held last frame out; masks are a
  new `CompositionBuilder+Masks.swift` with one wiring line.
- `app/Sources/AgentServer.swift` 807 (frozen): new tools join `creatorHandlers`
  (`AgentServer+CreatorJobs.swift`, CJ0 T8, CJ-8 (d)).
- `app/Sources/TimelineView.swift` 1704 (frozen): one stored property, CO9.
- `app/Sources/Playback.swift` 592, `app/Sources/ReverseRenderer.swift` 574: not touched.

### Decisions to record or amend

All go in `designs/spec/11-decisions/creator-jobs.md` (CJ0 opens it), each recorded before its
phase's code. CO-1…CO-9 and the amendments they carry are recorded in CO0.

**CO0's block (draft text).**

- **CO-1 — Remove Background uses Vision on the Mac.** Video uses
  `VNGeneratePersonSegmentationRequest` with a FRESH request per frame and the compute device
  pinned (CJ-32: the Neural Engine where present, else the GPU), never `.fast`, which carries
  state. Pictures may use `VNGenerateForegroundInstanceMaskRequest` (CO10); video never does,
  because it flickers. This adopts #124's D5. A matting model, shipped or downloaded, is allowed
  by CJ-1 and is not built in this road map; it is filed as a candidate only if JOB-60's verdict
  asks for it. Licence fact: Frame Job is Apache-2.0, so a GPL-3.0 or AGPL model (Robust Video
  Matting, Concat's) cannot ship in it. It needs no key (CJ-3).
- **CO-2 — The cutout is a property of the clip's own layer, not a matte track.** `video.cutout`
  on a media or still clip. A luma matte track holding a rendered mask movie has no link to the
  camera clip: a trim, split, slip, speed change, ramp or reverse of the camera moves one and not
  the other, and the person's outline slides off them (MT-2 is read per instant and per track pair
  by design). A per-layer mask follows the clip through every edit because it is fetched the way
  the picture is. Closed vocabulary; R5-1 and G-1 stand.
- **CO-3 — The mask reaches the compositor as a second composition track (provisional on
  CO-S2).** The plan gives each cut-out instance a MASK track whose segments copy its picture
  segments. Swift fills it from the cached mask chunks (CO-4). Each mask frame carries a
  presentation time chosen so that AVFoundation's hold — a track shows its latest sample at or
  before the requested time — shows, at every source frame, the mask of the NEAREST analysed
  source frame (ties to the earlier in the stream the segment reads): mask k takes over at the
  first source frame closer to its analysed frame than to mask k−1's. At every-frame analysis
  that is the source frame's own presentation time, so the hold is exact; at a capped rate the
  nearest mask is shown. A segment that crosses a chunk boundary is cut at that boundary in
  source ticks, and each part is placed by the picture segment's own linear map, computed in
  ticks and converted once (`fill`'s cursor rule). Mask tracks take ids from a range of their
  own (from 2001), so a project with no cutout has a byte-identical plan, and they count toward
  the eight-decoder warning. If CO-S2 fails this route, the fallback is a per-media mask pack
  looked up through the composition track's own segment mapping, and this entry is rewritten
  before CO2a.
- **CO-4 — Masks are an analysis kind on CJ2a's lane and store.** (a) The kinds are `masks`
  (Standard) and `masks_best` (Best, only if CO-S1 keeps it): quality is part of the kind, so a
  project with both qualities on one media keeps both. (b) The store is CJ-22's:
  `cache/analysis/masks/<media id>.json` holds the runs and the `AnalysisStamp` (source identity
  with no path, the kind's version, a digest of the request, its revision, the rate and the read
  size, the OS build, the compute device). (c) A run is one CHUNK of fixed source time, L seconds
  from source 0 (L from CO-S2; 10 s until it reports), so a window asks chunk by chunk and each
  chunk is a hit or a miss on its own (CJ-22's run rule, unchanged). Each run records
  `subject_found` (CO-5). (d) A run's payload is the chunk's mask movie,
  `cache/analysis/masks/<media id>/<k>.mov`, its samples at chunk-relative source times in the
  source track's own timescale, written through `CacheLedger.publish` by `AnalysisStore`.
  (e) A reversed clip's mask is the forward masks mirrored, never a second analysis: chunk `r<k>.mov`
  is forward chunk k read backwards with each time mirrored through `ReverseMirror` (D4-6 stands),
  made without Vision and published beside it. (f) Masks are in DISPLAY orientation (CJ-22,
  CJ-23), because Vision sees the reader's upright frame. (g) `get_media_analysis {media, kind:
  "masks"}` runs or reuses the kind for a window like any kind and answers its runs (`from`, `to`,
  `subject_found`, frame count) and the stamp, never pixels. (h) The package carries the folder as
  it carries `cache/reversed/`. Nothing promises byte-identical regeneration on another Mac; a
  proof compares against the cache, never a recomputation (E9's rule). **Clarifies CJ-22:** "a
  payload file" may be one per run, in a folder named by the media id beside the JSON. **Amends
  CJ-51:** the kept media's caches copied into a new project include `cache/analysis/` whole, the
  masks and their mirrored chunks with it.
- **CO-5 — "No person found" is decided per clip window.** A clip whose analysed chunks found no
  subject (no mask with at least 0.5 % of its pixels above 127) draws uncut, and its status says
  "No person found". Once any chunk of its window finds one, every analysed frame honours its
  mask, so a person who walks out leaves an empty picture, as asked. This is E9's rule per window,
  kept so that ticking Remove Background on a screencast cannot erase it. Swift decides it from the
  runs' `subject_found`; the core never reads analysis (CJ-20).
- **CO-6 — A frame without its mask draws uncut; a file waits.** Pending, cancelled and failed
  chunks draw the clip uncut, never blank and never the slate. An export waits for every chunk its
  range needs, through the export's one door for offline renders (`Exporter.withRampAudio`), and
  fails with `cutoutFailed` naming the clip when one fails. `render_frame` and File ▸ Save Frame…
  write files that a person or agent keeps, so they wait up to 30 s for the chunks their one
  frame needs; past that they draw the clip uncut and say so (`render_frame` in a sentence before
  its last, Save Frame in an informational sheet after saving). The eyedropper and the look

### Spikes

Each rule is fixed here and hashed before its run (CJ-7): instruments land under
`tools/proof/cutout_spike/`, next to the E9 instruments they extend, and each run's
`results.json` stores the SHA-256 of `designs/creator-jobs.md` as `rule_sha256`. Each runs on the
owner's Mac on AC power (`pmset` first), its verdict and numbers in CO0's record (CO-S3's in
CO4's when deferred).

- **CO-S1 — Which segmentation, at what rate and read size.**
  Question: which Vision request, rate and read size give the best outline per second of analysis
  on talking-head footage, and does a portrait source read upright (CJ-23's display orientation)
  cut as well as a landscape one?
  Candidates: person `.balanced`, person `.accurate`, `VNGeneratePersonInstanceMaskRequest` with
  `generateScaledMaskForImage`; each at every source frame (capped at 30 masks a second of
  source), at 15 and at 10 a second; frames read at the source's size and at a long side of 1920.
  Truth: S-KEY1's keyed composites ("Samples and fixtures").
  Measured on every truth frame against the mask the compositor would show there (CO-3's
  nearest-hold rule, so a capped rate's lag counts):
  J = mean IoU of mask > 0.5 against truth > 0.5;
  B = mean |mask − truth| inside an 8 px band around the true edge, at 1080p;
  B on the gesture segment;
  flicker = mean consecutive-mask difference on the still segment;
  realtime factor = source seconds per wall second for read, Vision and mask write together, at
  1080p30 and 4K30, pinned to the Neural Engine.
  Also: S-KEY1's composite re-tagged with a 90° rotation matrix (a portrait source with truth),
  and the first Vision call of a fresh process (E9's compile cost, recorded with no rule).
  **Rule.**
  (a) A candidate whose flicker exceeds 2 levels is out.
  (b) The rate is every frame, unless B on the gesture segment at 15 a second is within 5 % of B
  at every frame (then 15), and again at 10 a second within 5 % (then 10).
  (c) **Standard** is the fastest remaining candidate that runs at least 1.0× realtime at 1080p30
  at that rate and whose J is within 0.02 of the best J. If none reaches 1.0×, the rate steps
  down (every frame → 15 → 10) and (c) is applied again. If none reaches 1.0× at 10 a second,
  Standard is the fastest candidate within 0.02 J at 10 a second, and its realtime factor is
  recorded as a risk in the road map.
  (d) **Best** is the candidate with the lowest B, kept only if its B is at least 15 % below
  Standard's and it runs at least 0.25× realtime. Otherwise there is no Best, and no Quality
  control is built.
  (e) The read size is a long side of 1920 for a larger source when J and B there are within
  0.005 and 2 % of the source size's; otherwise the source size.
  (f) The rotated composite's J is within 0.01 of the unrotated composite's. If not, STOP: CJ-23
  is amended before CO1 to read coded frames and pass the orientation to Vision.
  If S-KEY1 has not arrived by CO0, (c) runs for speed alone on the E9 fixtures and S-TH1 if
  present, Standard is person `.balanced` at the fastest rate (every frame, 15, 10) that reaches
  1.0× realtime (E9 chose `.balanced` at 10 masks a second), and (b), (d), (e) and (f) run when
  S-KEY1 arrives, before CO4.

- **CO-S2 — How the mask reaches the compositor.**
  Question: does a mask movie inserted as a second composition track arrive registered, exact,
  small and cheap enough to build and play?
  Instrument: a probe compiled from `app/Sources` through `tools/proof/swift_build.py` (the mask
  track and `texture(4)` do not exist before CO2a). For each edit below it takes the core's plan
  of a project built through the FFI, adds by hand a mask track whose segments copy the picture
  segments, fills both through `CompositionBuilder.fill`, and reads every frame through a probe
  compositor — a subclass of the compositor class the project would use — that fetches both
  tracks' buffers per request. Frame counts come from the probe's own `AVPlayer` over the same
  composition.
  Fixture: a synthetic movie whose frame k carries its index as a bar code, and mask chunks written
  from it with chunk-relative times by CO-3's nearest-hold rule; a bar code reads back which mask
  frame arrived with which picture frame.
  Tried: HEVC 8-bit 4:2:0 full range with the mask in luma, then ProRes 422 Proxy; chunk lengths
  5, 10 and 30 s.
  **Rule.** The mask track (CO-3) is kept when all six hold:
  (1) **Registration.** Every frame shows the mask of the nearest analysed source frame (ties to
  the earlier in the stream its segment reads), at every-frame analysis and at 15 a second, across:
  a trim; ×0.5; ×2; ×1.37 with a chunk boundary inside the segment; a speed ramp that crosses a
  chunk boundary; a freeze frame; a reversed clip (its mirrored chunks, CO-4 (e)); a split; a clip
  inside a nest; a cross-dissolve; and an HLG variable-frame-rate source (S-TH1 when present, an
  `ffmpeg`-made HLG VFR fixture otherwise).
  (2) **Colour path.** The value the probe compositor reads differs from the DECODED mask by at
  most 1/255 at every pixel, in an SDR and an HLG composition, under the compositor class each
  would be built with. If the plain class conforms the mask, a composition with a mask track is
  built with `ConvertingCompositor` and (2) is measured again under it.
  (3) **Codec loss.** The decoded masks' IoU against Vision's own masks (both > 0.5) is at least
  0.995, and their mean |difference| inside the 8 px edge band at most 3 levels.
  (4) **Size.** At most 15 MB per minute of 30 fps source at Standard.
  (5) **Playback.** A 1080p30 camera with its mask track over a 4K screen recording composes, over
  20 s that cross at least five chunk boundaries, at least 99 % of the frames it composes without
  the mask track.
  (6) **Build.** `CompositionBuilder.build` of a 60-minute camera cut into 120 clips, every one cut
  out, takes at most 100 ms more (median of 10) than the same build without mask tracks.
  The chunk length L is the shortest of 5, 10 and 30 s that passes (5) and (6) and whose
  per-chunk fixed cost (the writer session, the file) adds under 5 % to analysis time per minute;
  the encoding is the smaller of the two that pass. Otherwise the per-media mask pack is measured
  on (1), (2), (5) and (6) and kept if it passes. If neither passes, CO stops after CO1 and the
  owner is asked.

- **CO-S3 — Whether the edge needs refinement, and which** (at CO0 when S-KEY1 exists, else at
  CO4's start).
  Question: how much does an edge-aware upsample of a 512×384 mask improve the outline at 1080p and
  4K, and what does it cost per frame?
  Candidates:
  r0, bilinear sampling and a smoothstep remap (the edge and feather controls);
  r1, a joint bilateral upsample inside the layer stage (3×3 mask texels weighted by the picture's
  colour distance, read as `KeyReading` reads);
  r2, a guided filter in a pass before the destination, at twice the mask's size.
  Instrument: a standalone Metal probe over S-KEY1's frames and their masks.
  Measured: B (as in CO-S1) on S-KEY1's composites, and cost per frame, full-frame, at 1080p and
  4K (200 frames a sample, three interleaved runs, the median of medians — MT0's method).
  **Rule.** The cheapest candidate whose B is at most 1.1 × the lowest B ships, provided it costs
  at most 1.0 ms at 1080p and 3.0 ms at 4K above r0. If r1 and r2 both miss the cost bound, r0
  ships and the better one is filed with its numbers.

- **CO-S4 — The analysis beside playback.**
  Question: does mask analysis at utility QoS drop preview frames?
  Instrument: CO-S1's instrument as a SEPARATE process under `taskpolicy -c utility`, analysing
  S-TH1 (or the E9 push-in) at Standard on the Neural Engine, while the Release app's
  `play_preview` plays a 1080p30 project for 20 s. The app's own lane does not exist yet; the
  Neural Engine and the decoders are shared system-wide, which is what is measured.
  Measured: frames composed with the instrument idle, then running; three runs each.
  **Rule.** If the median composed count falls by more than 2 %, `AnalysisLane` pauses while any
  transport plays and resumes when none does (CO-9, amending CJ-21); otherwise it runs throughout.
  CO1 builds what the verdict chose.

### Risks

- **Edges.** Balanced masks are 512×384 stretched over the frame; hair and fast hands may look cut
  with scissors. CO-S3 bounds what refinement buys and JOB-60 is the owner's verdict. If it is
  "not good enough", the remedy is a matting-model candidate (CO-1), which must carry a licence
  an Apache-2.0 app can ship.
- **Vision misses** backlit, from-behind and small figures (E9 §5b). The status says "No person
  found" for a window; a partial miss mid-clip shows as a missing arm.
- **Analysis time.** At every frame, Standard may run near or below 1× realtime; CO-S1 (c) steps
  the rate down to keep 1×, and if even 10 a second misses it the figure is recorded as a risk. An
  hour of camera is then about an hour of background work. Chunks limit it to the windows clips
  use.
- **Cache size.** CO-S2 bounds Standard at 15 MB per minute; Best may be several times that.
- **The mask track's colour.** A composition must not colour-manage a mask frame. CO-S2 (2)
  measures it per compositor class; a failure moves CO-3 to the fallback.
- **Decoders and builds.** Each cut-out instance adds a decode, and each chunk an asset per build.
  The eight-decoder warning counts mask tracks; CO-S2 (5) and (6) bound playback and build cost
  and choose the chunk length.
- **Masks differ across Macs.** GPU and ANE differ by up to 25 levels. A package carries its
  masks; a Mac that regenerates them may draw a slightly different edge. Proofs compare against
  cached masks.
- **The uniform block.** CO-8's size depends on whether CU's group lands first; the integrator
  renumbers it with the proofs' pins.
- **Layouts against existing placement.** A switch replaces the base placement of every role clip
  starting before the next layout action; a camera placed by hand there is overwritten unless
  `through` bounds the reach (the landing always passes it). Zooms and moving actions are refused
  and nested (CO-62); a nested screen loses rounded corners, because a nest clip's radius reaches
  no layer (`nest.rs:382`). A layout action deleted at a clip's head leaves its base and loses its
  marker, so an earlier switch can then reach over it.
- **Bet interactions.** Bet 1's cuts split every unlocked track; a split's second half takes the
  evaluated layout as its base, so a switch holds across cuts. Bet 1 shows words inside a nest as
  not editable, and CO-62 may nest picture clips; it never nests the microphone. Bet 2's cursor
  rides in the screen clip's layer (CU-4), so it moves with the screen and its nest. CU's Auto Zoom
  on a screen in `side_by_side` solves its regions against the whole canvas, not the box; the
  remedy is the same nest. Bet 3's vertical version should use `stacked` for screen-and-camera
  pairs rather than reframing each clip.
- **API drift.** If Apple deprecates the `VN*` segmentation classes in favour of the `async`-only
  Swift API (as `NSCursor.currentSystem` was deprecated), the analyser needs the `async`
  confinement W-8 allows, in `MediaImporter.swift` or a decision that widens it.
- **Licences.** Concat, Cap and OpenScreen code, shaders and models are not opened or carried over.

### Not in this bet

What this bet does not build; each is allowed by CJ-1 and may be a later road map.

- Replacing or blurring the background with something else as one command. It is already a
  composition (cutout plus Add Background or a blurred copy behind) and can be a later preset.
- Tracking or choosing one person among several, a brush to correct the mask, and rotoscoping.
- Non-person cutout on video (it flickers, E9 §5b).
- A cut-out live preview in the recorder panel, and anything that changes how the camera records.
  The system's own camera effects (Portrait, background replacement in Control Center) bake into
  the file when the creator turns them on, and Frame Job neither reads nor toggles them.
- Layouts with more than one camera or a grid of guests (bet 5's ground), a layout lane separate
  from actions, and layout shapes beyond square, rounded and circle.
- Face-tracking zoom on the camera, eye contact and retouching.
- A shipped or downloaded matting model (CO-1: a candidate only on JOB-60's verdict).

Prefix CO. Phases CO0, CO1, CO2a, CO2b, CO3…CO10; CO2a and CO2b share CO2's decision block
(CJ-7). Phase COn owns decisions CO-n0…CO-n9 (CO0 owns CO-1…CO-9). Spikes CO-S1…CO-S4. Manual
checks JOB-60…JOB-65 (numbers provisional; the integrator renumbers). Format bumps are written
"format N (provisional)": RC_FORMAT_VERSION is 37 at `d0661e5d` (`core/src/format.rs:18`), and each
bump is renumbered when its phase lands (CJ-6). Handoff directories are
`~/.claude/litecode/framejob/cj-co0`, `cj-co1`, `cj-co2a`, `cj-co2b`, `cj-co3` … `cj-co10`.

### Goal

A creator who records themselves gets four things on the camera clip that today need a green
screen or another app.

- **Remove Background.** One checkbox on a camera clip cuts the person out of their room. The
  segmentation runs on the Mac through Apple's Vision framework, on the road map's analysis lane,
  and is cached in the package. The edge can be shrunk, grown and softened. The drop shadow
  follows the person's outline. The camera keeps everything else Frame Job gives a clip: grading,
  LUTs, Camera Log, HDR, actions.
- **Text Behind Subject.** A title sits between the person and their background: the person's
  head passes in front of the words. It works over the camera's own room and over a screen
  recording behind a cut-out camera.
- **Camera layouts.** Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸ and a Layout section switch the camera at the
  playhead, with an eased move, between a corner picture (square, rounded or a circle), side by
  side, stacked for a vertical canvas, camera full and screen only. Each switch is an ordinary
  action on the camera clip and the screen clip, which the creator can drag, retime or delete on
  the action lane. The recorder offers the same layout at record time, and can land the camera
  with its background removed.
- **Hide the camera while silent.** The camera fades out while the microphone is silent and back
  in before speech resumes, read from the speech spans Frame Job already detects on the Mac.

Every control has an MCP mirror, so "put me in a circle bottom-left from 1:20, and hide me while I
type" is a sentence an agent can carry out in the calls a person's clicks make.

### Owner's answers applied

The owner's answers of 2026-11-01, as the orchestrator reads them for this bet. Each is a default
the owner can change.

- **"Add all: 1-6."** Bet 6 is in, as phases CO0…CO10 of road map "creator-jobs", in lane B after
  CU's phases (cj.md "Lane plan").
- **"Remove all explicit non-goals."** CJ-1 lifts spec §1's "ML or heavy pixel work outside the
  compositor's one pass". This bet uses the lift: Vision analysis on the analysis lane, and a
  mask sampled in the layer pass. Shipping or downloading a matting model is allowed by CJ-1 and
  is not built here; it becomes a filed candidate only if the owner's verdict on Vision's edges
  (JOB-60) is "not good enough". One licence fact bounds that candidate: Frame Job is
  Apache-2.0 (`LICENSE`), so code or weights under GPL-3.0 (Robust Video Matting's release) or
  AGPL (Concat's) cannot ship in it. That is a fact about licences, not a scope rule. Optical
  flow and stabilisation are allowed by CJ-1; nothing here needs them.
- **"The recorder can ask for input monitoring."** Not used by this bet. The recorder's camera
  rows gain a Layout pop-up and a checkbox (CO8), and neither needs a new grant.
- **The key rule (CJ-3).** Nothing in this bet needs a language model or a cloud model. Person

**CO0's block (draft text).**

- **CO-1 — Remove Background uses Vision on the Mac.** Video uses

  asks for it. Licence fact: Frame Job is Apache-2.0, so a GPL-3.0 or AGPL model (Robust Video

  on a media or still clip. A luma matte track holding a rendered mask movie has no link to the
  camera clip: a trim, split, slip, speed change, ramp or reverse of the camera moves one and not
  the other, and the person's outline slides off them (MT-2 is read per instant and per track pair

  the picture is. Closed vocabulary; R5-1 and G-1 stand.

  segments. Swift fills it from the cached mask chunks (CO-4). Each mask frame carries a
  presentation time chosen so that AVFoundation's hold — a track shows its latest sample at or
  before the requested time — shows, at every source frame, the mask of the NEAREST analysed
  source frame (ties to the earlier in the stream the segment reads): mask k takes over at the
  first source frame closer to its analysed frame than to mask k−1's. At every-frame analysis
  that is the source frame's own presentation time, so the hold is exact; at a capped rate the
  nearest mask is shown. A segment that crosses a chunk boundary is cut at that boundary in
  source ticks, and each part is placed by the picture segment's own linear map, computed in
  ticks and converted once (`fill`'s cursor rule). Mask tracks take ids from a range of their
  own (from 2001), so a project with no cutout has a byte-identical plan, and they count toward
  the eight-decoder warning. If CO-S2 fails this route, the fallback is a per-media mask pack
  looked up through the composition track's own segment mapping, and this entry is rewritten
  before CO2a.
- **CO-4 — Masks are an analysis kind on CJ2a's lane and store.** (a) The kinds are `masks`
  (Standard) and `masks_best` (Best, only if CO-S1 keeps it): quality is part of the kind, so a
  project with both qualities on one media keeps both. (b) The store is CJ-22's:
  `cache/analysis/masks/<media id>.json` holds the runs and the `AnalysisStamp` (source identity
  with no path, the kind's version, a digest of the request, its revision, the rate and the read
  size, the OS build, the compute device). (c) A run is one CHUNK of fixed source time, L seconds
  from source 0 (L from CO-S2; 10 s until it reports), so a window asks chunk by chunk and each
  chunk is a hit or a miss on its own (CJ-22's run rule, unchanged). Each run records
  `subject_found` (CO-5). (d) A run's payload is the chunk's mask movie,
  `cache/analysis/masks/<media id>/<k>.mov`, its samples at chunk-relative source times in the
  source track's own timescale, written through `CacheLedger.publish` by `AnalysisStore`.
  (e) A reversed clip's mask is the forward masks mirrored, never a second analysis: chunk `r<k>.mov`
  is forward chunk k read backwards with each time mirrored through `ReverseMirror` (D4-6 stands),
  made without Vision and published beside it. (f) Masks are in DISPLAY orientation (CJ-22,
  CJ-23), because Vision sees the reader's upright frame. (g) `get_media_analysis {media, kind:
  "masks"}` runs or reuses the kind for a window like any kind and answers its runs (`from`, `to`,

  it carries `cache/reversed/`. Nothing promises byte-identical regeneration on another Mac; a

  masks and their mirrored chunks with it.

  subject (no mask with at least 0.5 % of its pixels above 127) draws uncut, and its status says
  "No person found". Once any chunk of its window finds one, every analysed frame honours its
  mask, so a person who walks out leaves an empty picture, as asked. This is E9's rule per window,
  kept so that ticking Remove Background on a screencast cannot erase it. Swift decides it from the
  runs' `subject_found`; the core never reads analysis (CJ-20).

  chunks draw the clip uncut, never blank and never the slate. An export waits for every chunk its
  range needs, through the export's one door for offline renders (`Exporter.withRampAudio`), and

  frame needs; past that they draw the clip uncut and say so (`render_frame` in a sentence before
  its last, Save Frame in an informational sheet after saving). The eyedropper and the look
  gallery draw what the preview draws and do not wait. **Amends CJ-27:** a kind whose result a
  render substitutes (the masks) shows no Analyzing sheet: the person keeps editing, the frame
  draws uncut while pending, and the clip's Background section says what is happening (CO3). A
  command that needs the masks to PLAN an edit (CO7's centroid) reads only what is cached.

  Log converts, or whose track is HLG or PQ, is analysed as an SDR project shows it (GR-21's

### Spikes

Each rule is fixed here and hashed before its run (CJ-7): instruments land under
`tools/proof/cutout_spike/`, next to the E9 instruments they extend, and each run's
`results.json` stores the SHA-256 of `designs/creator-jobs.md` as `rule_sha256`. Each runs on the
owner's Mac on AC power (`pmset` first), its verdict and numbers in CO0's record (CO-S3's in
CO4's when deferred).

- **CO-S1 — Which segmentation, at what rate and read size.**
  Question: which Vision request, rate and read size give the best outline per second of analysis
  on talking-head footage, and does a portrait source read upright (CJ-23's display orientation)
  cut as well as a landscape one?
  Candidates: person `.balanced`, person `.accurate`, `VNGeneratePersonInstanceMaskRequest` with
  `generateScaledMaskForImage`; each at every source frame (capped at 30 masks a second of
  source), at 15 and at 10 a second; frames read at the source's size and at a long side of 1920.
  Truth: S-KEY1's keyed composites ("Samples and fixtures").
  Measured on every truth frame against the mask the compositor would show there (CO-3's
  nearest-hold rule, so a capped rate's lag counts):
  J = mean IoU of mask > 0.5 against truth > 0.5;
  B = mean |mask − truth| inside an 8 px band around the true edge, at 1080p;
  B on the gesture segment;
  flicker = mean consecutive-mask difference on the still segment;
  realtime factor = source seconds per wall second for read, Vision and mask write together, at
  1080p30 and 4K30, pinned to the Neural Engine.
  Also: S-KEY1's composite re-tagged with a 90° rotation matrix (a portrait source with truth),
  and the first Vision call of a fresh process (E9's compile cost, recorded with no rule).
  **Rule.**
  (a) A candidate whose flicker exceeds 2 levels is out.
  (b) The rate is every frame, unless B on the gesture segment at 15 a second is within 5 % of B
  at every frame (then 15), and again at 10 a second within 5 % (then 10).
  (c) **Standard** is the fastest remaining candidate that runs at least 1.0× realtime at 1080p30
  at that rate and whose J is within 0.02 of the best J. If none reaches 1.0×, the rate steps
  down (every frame → 15 → 10) and (c) is applied again. If none reaches 1.0× at 10 a second,
  Standard is the fastest candidate within 0.02 J at 10 a second, and its realtime factor is
  recorded as a risk in the road map.
  (d) **Best** is the candidate with the lowest B, kept only if its B is at least 15 % below
  Standard's and it runs at least 0.25× realtime. Otherwise there is no Best, and no Quality
  control is built.
  (e) The read size is a long side of 1920 for a larger source when J and B there are within
  0.005 and 2 % of the source size's; otherwise the source size.
  (f) The rotated composite's J is within 0.01 of the unrotated composite's. If not, STOP: CJ-23
  is amended before CO1 to read coded frames and pass the orientation to Vision.
  If S-KEY1 has not arrived by CO0, (c) runs for speed alone on the E9 fixtures and S-TH1 if
  present, Standard is person `.balanced` at the fastest rate (every frame, 15, 10) that reaches
  1.0× realtime (E9 chose `.balanced` at 10 masks a second), and (b), (d), (e) and (f) run when
  S-KEY1 arrives, before CO4.

- **CO-S2 — How the mask reaches the compositor.**
  Question: does a mask movie inserted as a second composition track arrive registered, exact,
  small and cheap enough to build and play?
  Instrument: a probe compiled from `app/Sources` through `tools/proof/swift_build.py` (the mask
  track and `texture(4)` do not exist before CO2a). For each edit below it takes the core's plan
  of a project built through the FFI, adds by hand a mask track whose segments copy the picture
  segments, fills both through `CompositionBuilder.fill`, and reads every frame through a probe
  compositor — a subclass of the compositor class the project would use — that fetches both
  tracks' buffers per request. Frame counts come from the probe's own `AVPlayer` over the same
  composition.
  Fixture: a synthetic movie whose frame k carries its index as a bar code, and mask chunks written
  from it with chunk-relative times by CO-3's nearest-hold rule; a bar code reads back which mask
  frame arrived with which picture frame.
  Tried: HEVC 8-bit 4:2:0 full range with the mask in luma, then ProRes 422 Proxy; chunk lengths
  5, 10 and 30 s.
  **Rule.** The mask track (CO-3) is kept when all six hold:
  (1) **Registration.** Every frame shows the mask of the nearest analysed source frame (ties to
  the earlier in the stream its segment reads), at every-frame analysis and at 15 a second, across:
  a trim; ×0.5; ×2; ×1.37 with a chunk boundary inside the segment; a speed ramp that crosses a
  chunk boundary; a freeze frame; a reversed clip (its mirrored chunks, CO-4 (e)); a split; a clip
  inside a nest; a cross-dissolve; and an HLG variable-frame-rate source (S-TH1 when present, an
  `ffmpeg`-made HLG VFR fixture otherwise).
  (2) **Colour path.** The value the probe compositor reads differs from the DECODED mask by at
  most 1/255 at every pixel, in an SDR and an HLG composition, under the compositor class each
  would be built with. If the plain class conforms the mask, a composition with a mask track is
  built with `ConvertingCompositor` and (2) is measured again under it.
  (3) **Codec loss.** The decoded masks' IoU against Vision's own masks (both > 0.5) is at least
  0.995, and their mean |difference| inside the 8 px edge band at most 3 levels.
  (4) **Size.** At most 15 MB per minute of 30 fps source at Standard.
  (5) **Playback.** A 1080p30 camera with its mask track over a 4K screen recording composes, over
  20 s that cross at least five chunk boundaries, at least 99 % of the frames it composes without
  the mask track.
  (6) **Build.** `CompositionBuilder.build` of a 60-minute camera cut into 120 clips, every one cut
  out, takes at most 100 ms more (median of 10) than the same build without mask tracks.
  The chunk length L is the shortest of 5, 10 and 30 s that passes (5) and (6) and whose
  per-chunk fixed cost (the writer session, the file) adds under 5 % to analysis time per minute;
  the encoding is the smaller of the two that pass. Otherwise the per-media mask pack is measured
  on (1), (2), (5) and (6) and kept if it passes. If neither passes, CO stops after CO1 and the
  owner is asked.

- **CO-S3 — Whether the edge needs refinement, and which** (at CO0 when S-KEY1 exists, else at
  CO4's start).
  Question: how much does an edge-aware upsample of a 512×384 mask improve the outline at 1080p and
  4K, and what does it cost per frame?
  Candidates:
  r0, bilinear sampling and a smoothstep remap (the edge and feather controls);
  r1, a joint bilateral upsample inside the layer stage (3×3 mask texels weighted by the picture's
  colour distance, read as `KeyReading` reads);
  r2, a guided filter in a pass before the destination, at twice the mask's size.
  Instrument: a standalone Metal probe over S-KEY1's frames and their masks.
  Measured: B (as in CO-S1) on S-KEY1's composites, and cost per frame, full-frame, at 1080p and
  4K (200 frames a sample, three interleaved runs, the median of medians — MT0's method).
  **Rule.** The cheapest candidate whose B is at most 1.1 × the lowest B ships, provided it costs
  at most 1.0 ms at 1080p and 3.0 ms at 4K above r0. If r1 and r2 both miss the cost bound, r0
  ships and the better one is filed with its numbers.

- **CO-S4 — The analysis beside playback.**
  Question: does mask analysis at utility QoS drop preview frames?
  Instrument: CO-S1's instrument as a SEPARATE process under `taskpolicy -c utility`, analysing
  S-TH1 (or the E9 push-in) at Standard on the Neural Engine, while the Release app's
  `play_preview` plays a 1080p30 project for 20 s. The app's own lane does not exist yet; the
  Neural Engine and the decoders are shared system-wide, which is what is measured.
  Measured: frames composed with the instrument idle, then running; three runs each.
  **Rule.** If the median composed count falls by more than 2 %, `AnalysisLane` pauses while any
  transport plays and resumes when none does (CO-9, amending CJ-21); otherwise it runs throughout.
  CO1 builds what the verdict chose.

### Risks

- **Edges.** Balanced masks are 512×384 stretched over the frame; hair and fast hands may look cut
  with scissors. CO-S3 bounds what refinement buys and JOB-60 is the owner's verdict. If it is
  "not good enough", the remedy is a matting-model candidate (CO-1), which must carry a licence
  an Apache-2.0 app can ship.
- **Vision misses** backlit, from-behind and small figures (E9 §5b). The status says "No person
  found" for a window; a partial miss mid-clip shows as a missing arm.
- **Analysis time.** At every frame, Standard may run near or below 1× realtime; CO-S1 (c) steps
  the rate down to keep 1×, and if even 10 a second misses it the figure is recorded as a risk. An
  hour of camera is then about an hour of background work. Chunks limit it to the windows clips
  use.
- **Cache size.** CO-S2 bounds Standard at 15 MB per minute; Best may be several times that.
- **The mask track's colour.** A composition must not colour-manage a mask frame. CO-S2 (2)
  measures it per compositor class; a failure moves CO-3 to the fallback.
- **Decoders and builds.** Each cut-out instance adds a decode, and each chunk an asset per build.
  The eight-decoder warning counts mask tracks; CO-S2 (5) and (6) bound playback and build cost
  and choose the chunk length.
- **Masks differ across Macs.** GPU and ANE differ by up to 25 levels. A package carries its
  masks; a Mac that regenerates them may draw a slightly different edge. Proofs compare against
  cached masks.
- **The uniform block.** CO-8's size depends on whether CU's group lands first; the integrator
  renumbers it with the proofs' pins.
- **Layouts against existing placement.** A switch replaces the base placement of every role clip
  starting before the next layout action; a camera placed by hand there is overwritten unless
  `through` bounds the reach (the landing always passes it). Zooms and moving actions are refused
  and nested (CO-62); a nested screen loses rounded corners, because a nest clip's radius reaches
  no layer (`nest.rs:382`). A layout action deleted at a clip's head leaves its base and loses its
  marker, so an earlier switch can then reach over it.
- **Bet interactions.** Bet 1's cuts split every unlocked track; a split's second half takes the
  evaluated layout as its base, so a switch holds across cuts. Bet 1 shows words inside a nest as
  not editable, and CO-62 may nest picture clips; it never nests the microphone. Bet 2's cursor
  rides in the screen clip's layer (CU-4), so it moves with the screen and its nest. CU's Auto Zoom
  on a screen in `side_by_side` solves its regions against the whole canvas, not the box; the
  remedy is the same nest. Bet 3's vertical version should use `stacked` for screen-and-camera
  pairs rather than reframing each clip.
- **API drift.** If Apple deprecates the `VN*` segmentation classes in favour of the `async`-only
  Swift API (as `NSCursor.currentSystem` was deprecated), the analyser needs the `async`
  confinement W-8 allows, in `MediaImporter.swift` or a decision that widens it.
- **Licences.** Concat, Cap and OpenScreen code, shaders and models are not opened or carried over.

### Not in this bet

What this bet does not build; each is allowed by CJ-1 and may be a later road map.

- Replacing or blurring the background with something else as one command. It is already a
  composition (cutout plus Add Background or a blurred copy behind) and can be a later preset.
- Tracking or choosing one person among several, a brush to correct the mask, and rotoscoping.
- Non-person cutout on video (it flickers, E9 §5b).
- A cut-out live preview in the recorder panel, and anything that changes how the camera records.
  The system's own camera effects (Portrait, background replacement in Control Center) bake into
  the file when the creator turns them on, and Frame Job neither reads nor toggles them.
- Layouts with more than one camera or a grid of guests (bet 5's ground), a layout lane separate
  from actions, and layout shapes beyond square, rounded and circle.
- Face-tracking zoom on the camera, eye contact and retouching.
- A shipped or downloaded matting model (CO-1: a candidate only on JOB-60's verdict).

spikes.question: Which Vision request, rate and read size give the best outline per second of analysis on talking-head footage, and does a portrait source read upright cut as well as a landscape one?
spikes.rule: Measured against S-KEY1 truth with the mask the compositor would show (nearest-hold). (a) flicker > 2 levels out; (b) every frame unless gesture-segment B at 15/s within 5% (then 15), and at 10/s within 5% (then 10); (c) Standard = fastest remaining at >= 1.0x realtime at 1080p30 with J within 0.02 of best, stepping the rate down if none reaches 1.0x, else fastest within 0.02 J at 10/s with the factor recorded as a risk; (d) Best = lowest B, kept only if >= 15% below Standard's and >= 0.25x realtime; (e) read at long side 1920 when J and B are within 0.005 and 2% of source size; (f) rotated composite's J within 0.01 of unrotated, else STOP and amend CJ-23. Without S-KEY1: speed only, .balanced at the fastest rate reaching 1.0x. rule_sha256 stored.

spikes.question: Does a mask movie inserted as a second composition track arrive registered, exact, small and cheap enough to build and play?
spikes.rule: swift_build.py probe with hand-made mask segments and its own AVPlayer. Kept when all hold: (1) every frame shows the nearest analysed source frame's mask across trim, x0.5, x2, x1.37 across a chunk boundary, a ramp across a chunk boundary, freeze, reverse (mirrored chunks), split, nest, dissolve, HLG VFR source; (2) compositor read within 1/255 of the decoded mask in SDR and HLG under the class used (ConvertingCompositor if the plain class conforms); (3) decoded vs Vision masks IoU >= 0.995, edge-band difference <= 3 levels; (4) <= 15 MB/min; (5) >= 99% frames composed over 20 s crossing >= 5 chunk boundaries; (6) 60-min, 120-clip build <= +100 ms. Chunk length = shortest of 5/10/30 s passing (5), (6) and < 5% fixed cost; else per-media pack fallback; neither -> stop after CO1. rule_sha256 stored.

spikes.question: How much does an edge-aware upsample of a 512x384 mask improve the outline at 1080p and 4K, and what does it cost?
spikes.rule: Cheapest of r0/r1/r2 whose B <= 1.1x the lowest B ships, if it costs <= 1.0 ms at 1080p and <= 3.0 ms at 4K above r0; if r1 and r2 both miss the cost bound, r0 ships and the better is filed. Runs at CO0 when S-KEY1 exists, else at CO4's start. rule_sha256 stored.

spikes.question: Does mask analysis at utility QoS drop preview frames?
spikes.rule: Separate process (taskpolicy -c utility) analysing at Standard while the Release app's play_preview plays 1080p30 for 20 s, three runs each. If the median composed count falls by more than 2%, AnalysisLane pauses every job while any transport plays (amends CJ-21); otherwise it runs throughout. rule_sha256 stored.
